# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

```plantuml
}

    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}

    date : LocalDate

    contractor : boolean
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the trainer currently assigned to this session with a
         new trainer, strictly before the session's start date.
Algorithm:
  1. If newTrainer is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If date is null, return false.
  3. If today is not strictly before date (i.e., today >= date), return
     false.
  4. Set trainer to newTrainer.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, Person
Input: newTrainer : Trainer - the new trainer to assign; must be
       non-null.
       today : LocalDate - the current date; must be strictly earlier
       than this session's date.
Output: boolean - true if the trainer was successfully replaced; false
        otherwise (invalid arguments, no session date, or today not
        strictly before date).
Pre-condition: The Session instance exists; today is a valid LocalDate
               strictly earlier than date; a trainer (any reference) is
               currently assigned.
Post-condition: On success, trainer is set to newTrainer; on failure,
                trainer is unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to this session, which must be done strictly
         before the session's start date.
Algorithm:
  1. If t is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If date is null, return false.
  3. If today is not strictly before date (i.e., today >= date), return
     false (same-day or past assignments are not allowed).
  4. If trainer is already set, return false (use replaceTrainer to change
     an existing trainer).
  5. Set trainer to t.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: Session.trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, Person
Input: t : Trainer - the trainer to assign; must be non-null.
       today : LocalDate - the current date; must be strictly earlier
       than this session's date.
Output: boolean - true if the trainer was successfully assigned; false
        otherwise (invalid arguments, no session date, today not
        strictly before date, or a trainer already assigned).
Pre-condition: The Session instance exists; today is a valid LocalDate
               strictly earlier than date; trainer is currently null.
Post-condition: On success, trainer is set to t; on failure, trainer is
                unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Registers a participant for this session, ensuring no duplicate
         enrollments for the same participant.
Algorithm:
  1. If p is null, return false.
  2. If registeredParticipants already contains p (matched by participant
     id), return false (no duplicate enrollments).
  3. Add p to registeredParticipants.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Session.registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant, Person
Input: p : Participant - the participant to enroll; must be non-null and
       not already registered for this session.
       today : LocalDate - the current date (used for consistency with
       the registration workflow; this implementation does not impose
       a date-based restriction for participants).
Output: boolean - true if the participant was successfully registered;
        false otherwise (null participant or duplicate enrollment).
Pre-condition: The Session instance exists; p is a valid Participant not
               yet registered for this session.
Post-condition: On success, registeredParticipants contains p; on
                failure, registeredParticipants is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a sector, removing it from its current sector
         (if any) before adding it to the new one.
Algorithm:
  1. If courseId or sectorId is null/empty, return false.
  2. Find the course c in courses whose id equals courseId; if not found,
     return false.
  3. Find the sector s in sectors whose id equals sectorId; if not found,
     return false.
  4. If c.sector is not null and different from s, call
     c.sector.removeCourse(c) to detach c from its previous sector.
  5. Call s.addCourse(c) to attach c to the new sector.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: School.courses, School.sectors, Course.sector,
                  Sector.courses
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId : String - the unique id of the course to move; must
       reference an existing course in this school.
       sectorId : String - the unique id of the target sector; must
       reference an existing sector in this school.
Output: boolean - true if the course was successfully (re)assigned to the
        target sector; false if any id is invalid or a referenced
        course/sector does not exist.
Pre-condition: The School instance exists; both courseId and sectorId
               refer to existing course and sector within this school.
Post-condition: On success, the course's sector is the target sector and
                the course appears in that sector's courses list (and is
                no longer present in any previous sector's courses list);
                on failure, course/sector memberships are unchanged.

School::addCourse
Summary: Adds a new course to the school by providing a case-sensitive
         unique course id.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty (after trimming), return false.
  2. Iterate over courses; if any course has an id equal (case-sensitive)
     to the provided id, return false.
  3. Create a new Course with id, empty documents, null sector, and empty
     sessions.
  4. Add the new course to courses.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: School.courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: id : String - the unique case-sensitive identifier of the new
       course; must be non-null and not already used by an existing course.
Output: boolean - true if the course was successfully added; false
        otherwise.
Pre-condition: The School instance exists with a unique name; id is a
               non-null, non-empty String not currently used by any
               existing course in this school.
Post-condition: On success, courses contains a new Course with the given
                id; on failure, courses is unchanged.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector with a case-sensitive unique id and adds it
         to the school's list of sectors, returning the created sector.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty (after trimming), return null.
  2. Iterate over sectors; if any sector has an id equal (case-sensitive)
     to the provided id, return null.
  3. Create a new Sector with id and an empty courses list.
  4. Add the new sector to sectors.
  5. Return the created sector.
Related Features: School.sectors
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id : String - the unique case-sensitive identifier of the new
       sector; must be non-null and not already used by an existing
       sector.
Output: Sector - the newly created Sector on success; null if the id is
        invalid or already in use.
Pre-condition: The School instance exists; id is a non-null, non-empty
               String not currently used by any existing sector in this
               school.
Post-condition: On success, sectors contains the new Sector and the
                returned reference refers to it; on failure, sectors is
                unchanged and null is returned.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a referenced document from the course by removing it from
         the course's document list.
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. If documents does not contain doc (matched by reference/name), return
     false.
  3. Remove doc from documents.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to delete; must be non-null and
       currently present in this course's documents.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully removed; false
        otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists and currently references the
               given document.
Post-condition: On success, documents no longer contains the deleted
                document; on failure, documents is unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a referenced document to the course by appending it to the
         course's document list.
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. If documents already contains an element with the same name as doc,
     return false (avoid duplicate document names on the same course).
  3. Add doc to documents.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to upload; must be non-null and its
       name must not collide with an existing document name on this course.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully added; false
        otherwise (null document or duplicate document name).
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists in the school's catalog.
Post-condition: On success, documents contains the new Document; on
                failure, documents is unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session for this course on the specified date, ensuring
         that only one session exists per course per day, and returns the
         up-to-date list of sessions.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return the current sessions unchanged.
  2. Iterate over sessions; if any session has the same date, return the
     current sessions unchanged (no duplicate date allowed).
  3. Create a new Session with date, empty registeredParticipants, and
     null trainer.
  4. Append the new session to sessions.
  5. Return the up-to-date sessions list.
Related Features: Course.sessions
Related Classes: Session
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the new session in "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: List<Session> - the course's updated list of sessions, containing
        the new session when the addition was successful, or the original
        list when the date was already taken or invalid.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists; date is a valid LocalDate and
               no existing session of this course has the same date.
Post-condition: On success, sessions contains one additional Session with
                the provided date; on failure, sessions is unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels (removes) the session of this course that occurs on the
         given date, but only when it has no registered participants.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return false.
  2. Find the session s in sessions whose date equals the given date.
  3. If no such session is found, return false.
  4. If s.registeredParticipants is not empty, return false
     (sessions with participants cannot be removed).
  5. Remove s from sessions.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: Course.sessions
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the session to cancel, format
       "yyyy-MM-dd".
Output: boolean - true if the session was successfully removed; false if
        the date is null, the session does not exist, or the session has
        one or more registered participants.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists; date refers to an existing
               session of this course.
Post-condition: On success, the matching session is removed from
                sessions; on failure, sessions is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Course::removeDocument
Summary: Deletes a referenced document from the course by removing it from
         the course's document list.
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. If documents does not contain doc (matched by reference/name), return
     false.
  3. Remove doc from documents.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to delete; must be non-null and
       currently present in this course's documents.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully removed; false
        otherwise.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists and currently references the
               given document.
Post-condition: On success, documents no longer contains the deleted
                document; on failure, documents is unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Uploads a referenced document to the course by appending it to the
         course's document list.
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. If documents already contains an element with the same name as doc,
     return false (avoid duplicate document names on the same course).
  3. Add doc to documents.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: Course.documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to upload; must be non-null and its
       name must not collide with an existing document name on this course.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully added; false
        otherwise (null document or duplicate document name).
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists in the school's catalog.
Post-condition: On success, documents contains the new Document; on
                failure, documents is unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session for this course on the specified date, ensuring
         that only one session exists per course per day, and returns the
         up-to-date list of sessions.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return the current sessions unchanged.
  2. Iterate over sessions; if any session has the same date, return the
     current sessions unchanged (no duplicate date allowed).
  3. Create a new Session with date, empty registeredParticipants, and
     null trainer.
  4. Append the new session to sessions.
  5. Return the up-to-date sessions list.
Related Features: Course.sessions
Related Classes: Session
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the new session in "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Output: List<Session> - the course's updated list of sessions, containing
        the new session when the addition was successful, or the original
        list when the date was already taken or invalid.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists; date is a valid LocalDate and
               no existing session of this course has the same date.
Post-condition: On success, sessions contains one additional Session with
                the provided date; on failure, sessions is unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels (removes) the session of this course that occurs on the
         given date, but only when it has no registered participants.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return false.
  2. Find the session s in sessions whose date equals the given date.
  3. If no such session is found, return false.
  4. If s.registeredParticipants is not empty, return false
     (sessions with participants cannot be removed).
  5. Remove s from sessions.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: Course.sessions
Related Classes: Session, Participant
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the session to cancel, format
       "yyyy-MM-dd".
Output: boolean - true if the session was successfully removed; false if
        the date is null, the session does not exist, or the session has
        one or more registered participants.
Pre-condition: The Course instance exists; date refers to an existing
               session of this course.
Post-condition: On success, the matching session is removed from
                sessions; on failure, sessions is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

                unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Class Diagram
```plantuml
@startuml

title trainingSchool Model

class Course {
    id : String
    documents : List<Document>
    sector : Sector
    sessions : List<Session>
    addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
    addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
    cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
    removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
}
class Document {
    name : String
}
class Participant {
}
abstract class Person {
    id : String
}
class School {
    name : String
    courses : List<Course>
    sectors : List<Sector>
    addCourse(id : String) : boolean
    addSector(id : String) : Sector
    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}
class Sector {
    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Course --> "*" Document : documents
Course --> Sector : sector  'opposite: courses
Course *-- "*" Session : sessions
Participant --|> Person
School *-- "*" Course : courses
School *-- "*" Sector : sectors
Sector --> "*" Course : courses  'opposite: sector
Session --> "*" Participant : registeredParticipants
Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a sector by IDs, ensuring a course belongs to at most
         one sector at a time. Returns true on success, false if either ID is unknown.
Algorithm:
  1. Look up the Course with courseId in courses; if not found, return false.
  2. Look up the Sector with sectorId in sectors; if not found, return false.
  3. If course.sector is not null, call course.sector.removeCourse(course).
  4. Call newSector.addCourse(course) and return true.
Related Features: courses, sectors (and indirectly Course::sector, Sector::courses)
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input:
  - courseId (String) - identifier of the course to reassign.
  - sectorId (String) - identifier of the target sector.
Output: boolean - true if reassignment succeeded; false if either ID is unknown.
Pre-condition: courseId and sectorId each refer to an existing Course and Sector in this school.
Post-condition: The course is associated with the new sector, and any previous sector association is cleared.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector in the school with a unique ID and returns the created
         Sector instance. If the ID is empty or already used, returns null.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty (after trim), return null.
  2. Iterate sectors; if any sector's id equals id, return null.
  3. Create a new Sector with the given id, append to sectors, and return the new Sector.
Related Features: sectors
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id (String) - the unique sector identifier; non-null and non-empty.
Output: Sector - the newly created Sector, or null if creation failed.
Pre-condition: The id is not already in use by any existing sector in this school.
Post-condition: On non-null return, a new Sector with the given id is added to sectors.

School::addCourse
Summary: Creates a new course in the school with a case-sensitive unique ID. Returns
         true if the course is added; false if the ID is invalid, empty, or already used.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty (after trim), return false.
  2. Iterate courses; if any course's id equals id (case-sensitive), return false.
  3. Create a new Course with the given id, append to courses, and return true.
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: id (String) - the unique course identifier; case-sensitive; non-null and non-empty.
Output: boolean - true on success, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The id is not already in use by any existing course in this school.
Post-condition: On true, a new Course with the given id is added to courses. On false, courses is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

```plantuml
@startuml

    documents : List<Document>

}

    contractor : boolean
}
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Registers a participant for this session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments
         for the same participant. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If p is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If today is not strictly before date, return false.
  3. If registeredParticipants already contains p, return false.
  4. Add p to registeredParticipants and return true.
Related Features: date, registeredParticipants
Related Classes: Participant
Input:
  - p (Participant) - the participant to register; non-null.
  - today (LocalDate) - the current date; must be strictly earlier than date.
Output: boolean - true if registration succeeded, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: p is not already registered for this session; today is strictly earlier than the session date.
Post-condition: On true, p is contained in registeredParticipants. On false, the list is unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer of this session with a new trainer.
         The replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date
         (today < session.date). Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If newTrainer is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If today is not strictly before date, return false.
  3. If trainer is null, return false (there is nothing to replace).
  4. Set trainer to newTrainer and return true.
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
  - newTrainer (Trainer) - the replacement trainer; non-null.
  - today (LocalDate) - the current date; must be strictly earlier than date.
Output: boolean - true if the trainer was replaced, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: A trainer is already assigned to this session; today is strictly earlier than date; newTrainer is non-null and not the same as the current trainer.
Post-condition: On true, this session's trainer is newTrainer. On false, trainer is unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to this session. The assignment must be done strictly
         before the session's start date (today < session.date). Returns true on success.
Algorithm:
  1. If t is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If today is not strictly before date, return false.
  3. If trainer is already set and equals t, return true.
  4. Set trainer to t and return true.
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
  - t (Trainer) - the trainer to assign; non-null.
  - today (LocalDate) - the current date used for the start-date check; non-null.
Output: boolean - true if assignment succeeded, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: today is strictly earlier than date; session has no current trainer (or the same trainer is being re-assigned).
Post-condition: On true, this session's trainer is t.

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary: Detaches a course from this sector, if present.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, return without action.
  2. If courses contains course, remove it.
  3. If course.sector == this, set course.sector to null.
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: course (Course) - the course to detach; must be non-null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: course is currently associated with this sector.
Post-condition: course is no longer in this sector's courses list and course.sector is null.

Sector::addCourse
Summary: Associates a course with this sector. If the course is currently in another
         sector, it is removed from that sector first. After this call the course
         belongs to this sector.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, return without action.
  2. If course.sector is not null and is not this sector, call course.sector.removeCourse(course).
  3. If courses does not contain course, add it.
  4. Set course.sector to this.
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: course (Course) - the course to associate with this sector; must be non-null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: course is a valid Course instance.
Post-condition: course is in this sector's courses list and course.sector == this.

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary: Detaches a course from this sector, if present.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, return without action.
  2. If courses contains course, remove it.
  3. If course.sector == this, set course.sector to null.
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: course (Course) - the course to detach; must be non-null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: course is currently associated with this sector.
Post-condition: course is no longer in this sector's courses list and course.sector is null.

Sector::addCourse
Summary: Associates a course with this sector. If the course is currently in another
         sector, it is removed from that sector first. After this call the course
         belongs to this sector.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, return without action.
  2. If course.sector is not null and is not this sector, call course.sector.removeCourse(course).
  3. If courses does not contain course, add it.
  4. Set course.sector to this.
Related Features: courses
Related Classes: Course
Input: course (Course) - the course to associate with this sector; must be non-null.
Output: void
Pre-condition: course is a valid Course instance.
Post-condition: course is in this sector's courses list and course.sector == this.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels (removes) a scheduled session of this course on the specified date,
         but only if it has no registered participants. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return false.
  2. Find the session in sessions whose date matches the input date; if none found, return false.
  3. If the found session's registeredParticipants list is not empty, return false.
  4. Remove the session from sessions and return true.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session
Input: date (LocalDate) - the date of the session to cancel in yyyy-MM-dd format.
Output: boolean - true if the session was removed, false if not found or had participants.
Pre-condition: A session with the given date exists in this course; that session has no registered participants.
Post-condition: On true, the session is removed from sessions. On false, sessions is unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Removes a document from a course's document collection. Returns true on success,
         false if the document is null or not currently attached.
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. If documents does not contain doc, return false.
  3. Remove doc from documents and return true.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document) - the Document to detach; must be non-null and currently present in documents.
Output: boolean - true if removed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc exists in this course's documents list.
Post-condition: On true, doc is no longer in documents. On false, documents is unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Adds a document to a course's document collection. Returns true on success,
         false if the document is null or already attached to this course.
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. If documents already contains doc, return false.
  3. Append doc to documents.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: documents
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc (Document) - the Document instance to associate with the course; must be non-null and not already in documents.
Output: boolean - true when the document is added successfully; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc is a valid Document instance; this Course has been initialized.
Post-condition: When true, documents contains doc. When false, documents is unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session to a course on the specified date, ensuring at most one
         session per course per day, and returns the up-to-date list of sessions.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return the current sessions list unchanged.
  2. Iterate through sessions; if any session has a date equal to the input date, return current sessions list.
  3. Create a new Session with the given date and append it to sessions.
  4. Return the updated sessions list.
Related Features: sessions
Related Classes: Session
Input: date (LocalDate) - the session date in the format yyyy-MM-dd; must be non-null and unique per course per day.
Output: List<Session> - the course's current sessions list after the operation.
Pre-condition: date is a valid LocalDate; no existing session for this course has the same date.
Post-condition: A new Session with the given date is appended to sessions (or list is unchanged on failure).

```java
   * Input:

   *   - sectorId (String) - identifier of the target sector.
   * Output: boolean - true if reassignment succeeded; false if either ID is unknown.
   * Pre-condition: courseId and sectorId each refer to an existing Course and Sector in this school.
   * Post-condition: The course is associated with the new sector, and any previous sector association is cleared.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```
   * @generated NOT

  {
    Course course = null;
    for (Course c : getCourses())
    {
      if (courseId.equals(c.getId()))
      {
        course = c;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (course == null)
    {
      return false;
    }

    Sector newSector = null;
    for (Sector s : getSectors())
    {
      if (sectorId.equals(s.getId()))
      {
        newSector = s;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (newSector == null)
    {
      return false;
    }

    Sector currentSector = course.getSector();
    if (currentSector != null)
    {
      currentSector.removeCourse(course);
    }
    newSector.addCourse(course);
    return true;
  }

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::removeDocument
Summary: Removes a referenced document from the course's document list. Returns true on success, false otherwise (e.g., document not found or null input).
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. Iterate through the documents list to locate the entry matching the supplied doc.
  3. If not found, return false.
  4. Remove the document from the documents list.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to be removed from the course; must be non-null and currently present in the documents list.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully removed; false if the document is null or not present.
Pre-condition: The course exists; the supplied doc is non-null and exists in the course's documents list.
Post-condition: If successful, the document is no longer in the course's documents list; otherwise, the documents list remains unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Adds a referenced document (by name) to a course's document list. Returns true on successful addition, false otherwise (e.g., if the document is null, a document with the same name already exists in the course, or the document cannot be added).
Algorithm:
  1. If doc is null, return false.
  2. Iterate through the course's documents list.
  3. If a document with the same name (case-sensitive comparison) already exists, return false.
  4. Add doc to the documents list.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to be associated with the course; must be non-null and its name must be unique (case-sensitive) within the course's documents list.
Output: boolean - true if the document was added successfully, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: The course exists; the supplied doc is non-null; no existing document in the course's documents list shares the same name (case-sensitive).
Post-condition: If successful, the documents list of the course contains the new doc; otherwise, the documents list remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels (removes) a session on the specified date from the course. Only sessions that currently have no registered participants may be removed. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return false.
  2. Find the session in sessions whose date equals the given date.
  3. If no such session is found, return false.
  4. If the session has one or more registered participants, return false (cannot cancel).
  5. Remove the session from the sessions list.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the session to be cancelled; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null and correspond to an existing session in the course.
Output: boolean - true if the session was successfully cancelled; false if the date is null, no such session exists, or the session has registered participants.
Pre-condition: The course exists; the supplied date is non-null; a session with the given date exists in the course; the session has no registered participants.
Post-condition: If successful, the session is no longer part of the course's sessions list; otherwise, the sessions list remains unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session scheduled for the specified date to the course, ensuring no more than one session per day for the same course. Returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions.
Algorithm:
  1. If date is null, return the current sessions list unchanged.
  2. Iterate through the existing sessions list.
  3. If a session with the same date already exists, return the current sessions list (no duplicate added).
  4. Create a new Session with the given date, empty registeredParticipants, and null trainer.
  5. Add the new Session to the sessions list.
  6. Return the updated sessions list.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session
Input: date : LocalDate - the date on which the session is to be held; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null and not already present as a session date in this course.
Output: List<Session> - the up-to-date list of sessions of the course after the operation. May be empty if no sessions exist.
Pre-condition: The course exists; the supplied date is non-null; no existing session in the course is scheduled on the same date.
Post-condition: If the date was new, the sessions list contains a new Session with the given date and no participants or trainer; the returned list reflects the new state.

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary: Removes a given course from this sector and clears the course's sector reference if it points to this sector. Used when a course is being moved to a different sector.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, do nothing.
  2. Remove course from the courses list if present.
  3. If course.sector equals this sector, set course.sector to null.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>); side-effect: clears Course.sector
Related Classes: Course
Input: course : Course - the course to be removed from this sector; must be non-null.
Output: void - no return value.
Pre-condition: The sector exists; the supplied course is non-null.
Post-condition: The course is no longer in this sector's courses list, and if it previously pointed to this sector, its sector reference is now null.

Sector::addCourse
Summary: Associates a given course with this sector, setting the course's sector reference to this sector. Intended to be called as part of the school's assignCourseToSector workflow.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, do nothing.
  2. If courses list does not already contain the course, add it.
  3. Set the course's sector attribute to this sector.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>); side-effect: sets Course.sector
Related Classes: Course
Input: course : Course - the course to associate with this sector; must be non-null.
Output: void - no return value.
Pre-condition: The sector exists; the supplied course is non-null.
Post-condition: The course is added to this sector's courses list and the course's sector reference points to this sector.

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer of this session with a new trainer. The replacement must occur strictly before the session's start date. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If newTrainer is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If today is not strictly before this.date, return false.
  3. Set this.trainer to newTrainer (overwrites the previous trainer, if any).
  4. Return true.
Related Features: date (LocalDate), trainer (Trainer)
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
  - newTrainer : Trainer - the trainer to replace the current one; must be non-null.
  - today : LocalDate - the current date used for the time-bound check; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null and strictly earlier than the session's date.
Output: boolean - true if the trainer is successfully replaced; false if newTrainer is null, today is null, today is not strictly before the session date, or the replacement cannot be made.
Pre-condition: The session exists; newTrainer is non-null; today is a valid LocalDate strictly earlier than this session's date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session's trainer is set to newTrainer (any previous trainer is discarded); otherwise, the trainer attribute remains unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to this session. The assignment must occur strictly before the session's start date (today must be strictly earlier than the session date). Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If t is null or today is null, return false.
  2. If today is not strictly before this.date (i.e., today >= date), return false.
  3. Set this.trainer to t.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: date (LocalDate), trainer (Trainer)
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
  - t : Trainer - the trainer to be assigned to the session; must be non-null.
  - today : LocalDate - the current date used for the time-bound check; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null and strictly earlier than the session's date.
Output: boolean - true if the trainer is successfully assigned; false if t is null, today is null, today is not strictly before the session date, or the assignment cannot be made.
Pre-condition: The session exists; t is non-null; today is a valid LocalDate strictly earlier than this session's date.
Post-condition: If successful, the session's trainer is set to t; otherwise, the trainer attribute remains unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Registers a participant for this session, ensuring no duplicate enrollment for the same participant. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If p is null, return false.
  2. If registeredParticipants already contains p, return false (no duplicates).
  3. Add p to registeredParticipants.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: date (LocalDate), registeredParticipants (List<Participant>), trainer (Trainer)
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p : Participant - the participant to enroll in this session; must be non-null and not already registered.
Output: boolean - true if the participant is newly registered; false if p is null or already enrolled.
Pre-condition: The session exists; p is non-null; p is not already in the session's registeredParticipants list.
Post-condition: If successful, p is included in registeredParticipants; otherwise, the list remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector with a case-sensitive unique identifier and adds it to the school. Returns the newly created Sector instance, or null if the id is invalid or already exists.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty, return null.
  2. Iterate through the sectors list to check for an existing sector with the same id (case-sensitive).
  3. If a duplicate is found, return null.
  4. Create a new Sector with the given id and an empty courses list.
  5. Add the new Sector to the sectors list.
  6. Return the new Sector.
Related Features: sectors (List<Sector>), name (school identifier)
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id : String - the unique identifier of the new sector; must be non-null, non-empty, and case-sensitively unique within the school.
Output: Sector - the newly created Sector on success; null if the id is invalid or a duplicate.
Pre-condition: The school exists; the supplied id is a non-null, non-empty string that does not match any existing sector's id (case-sensitive).
Post-condition: If successful, the new Sector is included in the school's sectors list and is returned; otherwise, the sectors list remains unchanged and null is returned.

School::addCourse
Summary: Adds a new course with a case-sensitive unique identifier to the school. Returns true on success, false otherwise (e.g., null/empty id or duplicate id).
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty (after trimming), return false.
  2. Iterate through the school's courses list.
  3. If any existing course has the same id (case-sensitive comparison), return false.
  4. Create a new Course with the given id, empty documents list, null sector, and empty sessions list.
  5. Add the new Course to the courses list.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>), name (school identifier)
Related Classes: Course
Input: id : String - the unique identifier of the new course; must be non-null, non-empty, and case-sensitively unique within the school.
Output: boolean - true if the course was added; false if the id is invalid or already exists.
Pre-condition: The school exists; the supplied id is a non-null, non-empty string that does not match any existing course's id in this school (case-sensitive).
Post-condition: If successful, the school's courses list contains a new Course with the given id; otherwise, the courses list remains unchanged.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a new sector. A course belongs to exactly one sector; if the course is currently in a sector, it is removed from that sector first, then added to the new one. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If courseId or sectorId is null or empty, return false.
  2. Find the Course in the school's courses list whose id matches courseId (case-sensitive). If not found, return false.
  3. Find the Sector in the school's sectors list whose id matches sectorId (case-sensitive). If not found, return false.
  4. If the course's current sector is non-null, call removeCourse(course) on that sector.
  5. Call addCourse(course) on the target sector.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>), sectors (List<Sector>); accesses Course.sector
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input:
  - courseId : String - the unique identifier of the course to move; must be non-null, non-empty, and exist in the school.
  - sectorId : String - the unique identifier of the destination sector; must be non-null, non-empty, and exist in the school.
Output: boolean - true if the course is successfully assigned to the target sector; false if either id is invalid or the course/sector does not exist.
Pre-condition: The school exists; the course and sector identified by the supplied ids both exist in the school.
Post-condition: If successful, the course is no longer in its previous sector (if any) and is now associated with the target sector; otherwise, the course's sector assignment remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

```plantuml
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}

    contractor : boolean
}
```

# Operation Specifications
School::addCourse
Summary: Creates and adds a new course to the school's catalog using a
         case-sensitive unique ID. Returns true on success, false on
         duplicate id.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty, return false.
  2. Iterate over courses; if a course with the same id (case-sensitive
     string equality) exists, return false.
  3. Create a new Course with the given id, empty documents, empty
     sessions, and null sector.
  4. Add the new Course to courses.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>)
Related Classes: Course
Input: id : String - the case-sensitive unique course identifier.
Output: boolean - true if the course was added; false if id is invalid
        or already used by an existing course.
Pre-condition: id is a non-null, non-empty string that does not match
               (case-sensitively) any existing course id.
Post-condition: On success, courses contains the new Course; on failure,
                courses is unchanged.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector with a unique id and adds it to the
         school's sector list, returning the newly created Sector.
Algorithm:
  1. If id is null or empty, return null.
  2. Iterate over sectors; if a sector with the same id exists, return
     null.
  3. Create a new Sector with the given id and an empty courses list.
  4. Add the new Sector to sectors.
  5. Return the new Sector.
Related Features: sectors (List<Sector>)
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id : String - the unique sector identifier.
Output: Sector - the newly created Sector instance, or null on failure
        (invalid or duplicate id).
Pre-condition: id is a non-null, non-empty, unique string.
Post-condition: On success, sectors contains the new Sector which is
                returned; on failure, sectors is unchanged.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a (possibly new) sector. If the course is
         currently in another sector, it is removed from that sector
         first, then added to the target sector. Returns true on
         success, false on failure.
Algorithm:
  1. Look up the Course by courseId in courses; if not found, return
     false.
  2. Look up the Sector by sectorId in sectors; if not found, return
     false.
  3. If the course is already assigned to this sector, return true
     (idempotent).
  4. If the course has a current sector (course.sector != null), call
     course.sector.removeCourse(course) to detach it.
  5. Call targetSector.addCourse(course) to attach it.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses, sectors, Course.sector
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input:
  - courseId : String - the unique id of the course to assign.
  - sectorId : String - the unique id of the target sector.
Output: boolean - true on successful assignment; false if either id
        does not correspond to an existing course or sector.
Pre-condition: courseId refers to an existing Course; sectorId refers
               to an existing Sector; a course can belong to at most
               one sector at a time.
Post-condition: course.sector == targetSector; targetSector.courses
                contains the course; any previous sector no longer
                references the course.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary: Detaches a course from this sector and clears the course's
         back reference. Used when a course is reassigned or removed.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, do nothing.
  2. If courses does not contain course, do nothing.
  3. Remove course from courses.
  4. Set course.sector = null.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>)
Related Classes: Course
Input: course : Course - the course to detach from this sector.
Output: void
Pre-condition: course is currently assigned to this sector.
Post-condition: course is no longer in this sector's courses list and
                course.sector is null.

Sector::addCourse
Summary: Adds a course to this sector and updates the course's back
         reference. The course is assigned to this sector.
Algorithm:
  1. If course is null, do nothing.
  2. If courses already contains course, do nothing.
  3. Append course to courses.
  4. Set course.sector = this.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>)
Related Classes: Course
Input: course : Course - the course to be assigned to this sector.
Output: void
Pre-condition: course is non-null and not already in this sector.
Post-condition: course is in this sector's courses list and
                course.sector references this sector.

Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
```text
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

```plantuml
    id : String

    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}

    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Course --> Sector : sector  'opposite: courses
Course *-- "*" Session : sessions
Participant --|> Person
School *-- "*" Course : courses

Sector --> "*" Course : courses  'opposite: sector
Session --> "*" Participant : registeredParticipants
Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml
```
