# Operation Specifications
Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Enrolls a participant into this session, preventing duplicate
         enrollments for the same participant. The today parameter is
         accepted for time-based safety but the requirement only
         enforces uniqueness.
Algorithm:
  1. If p is null, return false.
  2. If registeredParticipants contains p, return false (duplicate
     enrollment).
  3. Append p to registeredParticipants.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: registeredParticipants (List<Participant>), date
                  (for context only)
Related Classes: Participant
Input:
  - p : Participant - the participant to enroll; must be non-null and
    identified by a unique Person id.
  - today : LocalDate - the current date; accepted for interface
    compatibility. The functional requirement only mandates duplicate
    prevention, so it is not used in the algorithm.
Output: boolean - true on successful registration; false if p is null
        or already registered.
Pre-condition: p is a valid Participant not already registered in
               registeredParticipants.
Post-condition: On success, registeredParticipants contains p; on
                failure, registeredParticipants is unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the currently assigned trainer of this session with
         a new one. The replacement must occur strictly before the
         session's start date.
Algorithm:
  1. If newTrainer is null, return false.
  2. If today is null or today is not strictly before date (i.e.,
     today >= date), return false.
  3. Set trainer = newTrainer.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
  - newTrainer : Trainer - the replacement trainer; must be non-null.
  - today : LocalDate - the current date, used to enforce the
    "strictly before session date" rule.
Output: boolean - true on successful replacement; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: newTrainer is non-null; today is strictly before the
               session's date.
Post-condition: On success, trainer references newTrainer; on failure,
                trainer is unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to this session, but only if the operation
         is performed strictly before the session's start date.
         (Replacement of an existing trainer is done via
         replaceTrainer; this operation assumes trainer is null.)
Algorithm:
  1. If t is null, return false.
  2. If today is null or today is not strictly before date (i.e.,
     today >= date), return false.
  3. If trainer is already set, return false (use replaceTrainer
     instead).
  4. Set trainer = t.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trainer, date
Related Classes: Trainer
Input:
  - t : Trainer - the trainer to assign; must be non-null.
  - today : LocalDate - the current date, used to enforce the
    "strictly before session date" rule.
Output: boolean - true on successful assignment; false otherwise.
Pre-condition: t is non-null; today is strictly before the session's
               date; this session currently has no trainer assigned.
Post-condition: On success, trainer references t; on failure, trainer
                is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::addCourse
Summary:
  Adds a new course to the school, identified by a case-sensitive unique ID.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the supplied id is non-null and non-empty.
  2. Check this.school.courses for any course whose id equals the supplied id using case-sensitive comparison.
  3. If a course with the same id already exists, return false.
  4. Otherwise, instantiate a new Course with the given id, empty documents list, null sector, and empty sessions list, add it to this.school.courses, and return true.
Related Features:
  - courses : List<Course>
Related Classes:
  Course
Input:
  id : String - the unique case-sensitive identifier of the new course; must be non-null and non-empty.
Output:
  boolean - true if the course was successfully created and added; false if the id is null/empty or already used (case-sensitively) by another course in the school.
Pre-condition:
  - The school instance exists.
  - The supplied id is non-null, non-empty, and not already used by any course in this.school.courses under case-sensitive comparison.
Post-condition:
  - On success: this.school.courses contains one additional Course with the given id, no sector, no sessions, and no documents.
  - On failure: this.school.courses remains unchanged.

School::addSector
Summary:
  Creates and adds a new sector to the school, identified by a unique ID.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the supplied id is non-null and non-empty.
  2. Check this.school.sectors for any sector whose id equals the supplied id.
  3. If a sector with the same id already exists, return that existing sector (to keep ids unique) or null based on policy; in this design we assume a new sector must have a unique id, so if a duplicate exists return null.
  4. Otherwise, instantiate a new Sector with the given id and an empty courses list, add it to this.school.sectors, and return the new sector.
Related Features:
  - sectors : List<Sector>
Related Classes:
  Sector
Input:
  id : String - the unique identifier of the new sector; must be non-null and non-empty.
Output:
  Sector - the newly created sector on success; null if the id is invalid or already used by another sector.
Pre-condition:
  - The school instance exists.
  - The supplied id is non-null, non-empty, and not already used by any sector in this.school.sectors.
Post-condition:
  - On success: this.school.sectors contains one additional Sector with the given id and an empty courses list.
  - On failure: this.school.sectors remains unchanged and null is returned.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary:
  Assigns a course to a sector, ensuring the course belongs to exactly one sector at a time by first removing it from its current sector (if any).
Algorithm:
  1. Validate both courseId and sectorId are non-null and non-empty.
  2. Locate the Course in this.school.courses whose id equals courseId and the Sector in this.school.sectors whose id equals sectorId.
  3. If either the course or the sector is not found, return false.
  4. If the course already has a sector (course.sector != null), invoke that sector's removeCourse(course) operation to detach it.
  5. Invoke the new sector's addCourse(course) operation to attach the course and set course.sector to the new sector.
  6. Return true.
Related Features:
  - courses : List<Course>
  - sectors : List<Sector>
Related Classes:
  Course, Sector
Input:
  courseId : String - the unique id of the course to assign; must be non-null and non-empty; case-sensitive.
  sectorId : String - the unique id of the target sector; must be non-null and non-empty.
Output:
  boolean - true if the course was successfully (re)assigned to the new sector; false if either id was not found.
Pre-condition:
  - The school instance exists.
  - A course with the given courseId exists in this.school.courses.
  - A sector with the given sectorId exists in this.school.sectors.
Post-condition:
  - The course belongs to exactly one sector, namely the one identified by sectorId.
  - Any previous sector no longer references the course; the new sector's courses list contains the course.
  - On failure, the course-sector relationship is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary:
  Removes a course from this sector's list of courses.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that the supplied course is non-null.
  2. If the course is present in this.sector.courses, remove it.
  3. If the removed course currently has its sector set to this, clear course.sector (set to null) to keep the invariant that a course belongs to at most one sector.
Related Features:
  - courses : List<Course>
Related Classes:
  Course
Input:
  course : Course - the course to detach from this sector; must be non-null.
Output:
  void - no return value.
Pre-condition:
  - The sector instance exists.
  - The supplied course is non-null.
Post-condition:
  - The course is no longer present in this.sector.courses.
  - If course.sector == this, then course.sector becomes null; otherwise course.sector is left to the caller's responsibility.

Sector::addCourse
Summary:
  Adds a course to this sector's list of courses.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that the supplied course is non-null.
  2. If the course is not already in this.sector.courses, add it to the list.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Sector::removeCourse
Summary:
  Removes a course from this sector's list of courses.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that the supplied course is non-null.
  2. If the course is present in this.sector.courses, remove it.
  3. If the removed course currently has its sector set to this, clear course.sector (set to null) to keep the invariant that a course belongs to at most one sector.
Related Features:
  - courses : List<Course>
Related Classes:
  Course
Input:
  course : Course - the course to detach from this sector; must be non-null.
Output:
  void - no return value.
Pre-condition:
  - The sector instance exists.
  - The supplied course is non-null.
Post-condition:
  - The course is no longer present in this.sector.courses.
  - If course.sector == this, then course.sector becomes null; otherwise course.sector is left to the caller's responsibility.

Related Features:

# Operation Specifications
Session::registerParticipant
Summary:
  Registers a participant for this session, preventing duplicate enrollments.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the supplied participant is non-null.
  2. Check this.session.registeredParticipants for the participant (by identity or unique id).
  3. If the participant is already registered, return false.
  4. Otherwise, add the participant to this.session.registeredParticipants and return true.
Related Features:
  - registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
Related Classes:
  Participant
Input:
  p : Participant - the participant to enroll; must be non-null and identified by Person.id.
  today : LocalDate - the current date (declared for symmetry with other session operations and possible future date checks); format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null. In the current requirements no date restriction is enforced, but the parameter is accepted.
Output:
  boolean - true if the participant was successfully registered; false if the participant is null or already registered for this session.
Pre-condition:
  - The session instance exists.
  - The supplied participant is non-null and not already in this.session.registeredParticipants.
Post-condition:
  - On success: this.session.registeredParticipants contains p.
  - On failure: this.session.registeredParticipants remains unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary:
  Replaces the current trainer of this session with a new trainer, allowed only strictly before the session's start date.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the supplied newTrainer is non-null and today is non-null.
  2. Compare this.session.date with today:
       - If today is strictly earlier than this.session.date (today < session.date), proceed.
       - Otherwise (today >= session.date, including same-day), return false.
  3. Set this.session.trainer to newTrainer and return true.
Related Features:
  - date : LocalDate
  - trainer : Trainer
Related Classes:
  Trainer
Input:
  newTrainer : Trainer - the trainer to assign in place of the current one; must be non-null.
  today : LocalDate - the current date used for the strict before check; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null.
Output:
  boolean - true if the trainer was successfully replaced; false if validation fails or today is not strictly before this.session.date.
Pre-condition:
  - The session instance exists.
  - The supplied newTrainer is non-null.
  - today is strictly earlier than this.session.date (same-day operations are not allowed).
Post-condition:
  - On success: this.session.trainer points to newTrainer; any previous trainer reference is replaced.
  - On failure: this.session.trainer remains unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary:
  Assigns a trainer to this session, allowed only strictly before the session's start date.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the supplied trainer is non-null and today is non-null.
  2. Compare this.session.date with today:
       - If today is strictly earlier than this.session.date (today < session.date), proceed.
       - Otherwise (today >= session.date, including same-day), return false.
  3. Set this.session.trainer to the supplied trainer and return true.
Related Features:
  - date : LocalDate
  - trainer : Trainer
Related Classes:
  Trainer
Input:
  t : Trainer - the trainer to assign; must be non-null.
  today : LocalDate - the current date used for the strict before check; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null.
Output:
  boolean - true if the trainer was successfully assigned; false if validation fails or today is not strictly before this.session.date.
Pre-condition:
  - The session instance exists.
  - The supplied trainer is non-null.
  - today is strictly earlier than this.session.date (same-day operations are not allowed).
Post-condition:
  - On success: this.session.trainer is set to t.
  - On failure: this.session.trainer remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::cancelSession
Summary:
  Cancels (removes) a session of this course for a given date, only if that session has no registered participants.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the input date is non-null.
  2. Locate the session in this.course.sessions whose date equals the input date.
  3. If no such session is found, return false.
  4. If the session is found, check its registeredParticipants list:
       a. If it is empty, remove the session from this.course.sessions and return true.
       b. If it is non-empty, do not remove the session and return false.
Related Features:
  - sessions : List<Session>
Related Classes:
  Session
Input:
  date : LocalDate - the date of the session to cancel; format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null.
Output:
  boolean - true if the session was successfully removed; false if no session was found for the date or if the session still has participants.
Pre-condition:
  - The course instance exists.
  - A session with the given date exists in this.course.sessions and has zero registered participants (for success).
Post-condition:
  - On success: the session is removed from this.course.sessions and is no longer reachable from the course.
  - On failure: this.course.sessions remains unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary:
  Attaches a referenced document to a course.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that the supplied document is not null and that the document is not already attached to this course.
  2. If validation passes, add the document to the documents list and return true.
  3. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features:
  - documents : List<Document>
Related Classes:
  Document
Input:
  doc : Document - the document to attach; must be non-null and identified by its name; no other constraints.
Output:
  boolean - true if the document was successfully added to the course; false otherwise (e.g., null document or duplicate).
Pre-condition:
  - The course instance exists.
  - The supplied document is non-null and is not already present in this.course.documents (compared by document name).
Post-condition:
  - On success: the document is appended to this.course.documents and no document is lost.
  - On failure: this.course.documents remains unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary:
  Detaches a referenced document from a course.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate that the supplied document is not null.
  2. Attempt to locate the document in this.course.documents (by identity or by document name).
  3. If found, remove it from this.course.documents and return true.
  4. If not found, return false.
Related Features:
  - documents : List<Document>
Related Classes:
  Document
Input:
  doc : Document - the document to detach; must be non-null; typically identified by its name.
Output:
  boolean - true if the document was found and removed; false otherwise (e.g., null document or document not attached).
Pre-condition:
  - The course instance exists.
  - The supplied document is non-null and is currently present in this.course.documents (for success).
Post-condition:
  - On success: the document is no longer present in this.course.documents.
  - On failure: this.course.documents remains unchanged.

Course::addSession
Summary:
  Adds a new session for a specific date to the course, ensuring no duplicate session exists for the same day, and returns the up-to-date list of sessions.
Algorithm:
  1. Validate the input date is non-null.
  2. Scan this.course.sessions; if a session with the same date already exists, do not add a new one.
  3. Otherwise, instantiate a new Session with the supplied date, an empty participants list, and a null trainer, then add it to this.course.sessions.
  4. Return this.course.sessions (whether or not a new session was added).
Related Features:
  - sessions : List<Session>
Related Classes:
  Session
Input:
  date : LocalDate - the date of the session in format "yyyy-MM-dd"; must be non-null.
Output:
  List<Session> - the current (up-to-date) list of sessions for the course; never null. If the date already had a session, the list is returned without modification.
Pre-condition:
  - The course instance exists.
  - The provided date is non-null and follows the "yyyy-MM-dd" format.
Post-condition:
  - If the date was new, the list contains one additional Session with no trainer and no registered participants.
  - If the date already had a session, the list is unchanged and contains no duplicate dates.

    }
    Course course = null;
    for (Course c : getCourses())
    {
      if (courseId.equals(c.getId()))
      {
        course = c;
        break;
      }
    }
    Sector sector = null;
    for (Sector s : getSectors())
    {
      if (sectorId.equals(s.getId()))
      {
        sector = s;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (course == null || sector == null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    Sector currentSector = course.getSector();
    if (currentSector != null)
    {
      currentSector.removeCourse(course);
    }
    sector.addCourse(course);
    course.setSector(sector);
    return true;
  }
